result_text:
I changed the `all_files.zip` export so it looks up and names each entry from the configured aspect name. It compiles, but I didn't run any tests or try the renamed-aspect case.

The change is in `DataExporter.java` in the `reports` module. The five hard-coded `aspect_*.txt` literals are gone. The code now takes the five scope aspects in the same order as before: main, test, generated, build and deployment, other. For each one it gets the file name from `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`, which is the same helper that writes the loose text files. That name is used both to read the file and as the zip entry name.

With the default configuration the entries stay `aspect_main.txt`, `aspect_test.txt`, `aspect_generated.txt`, `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt` and `aspect_other.txt`. With the renamed aspect, the fourth entry becomes `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`. Because the read no longer fails, `git-history.zip` is written as well when a `git-history.txt` exists.

I left `LandscapeAnalyzer.java` alone. It reads the same five file names as literals (lines 280–284), so a renamed aspect likely affects it too. That was outside this task, so I didn't touch it.
